title.en: I've lived here for ten years

goal.sl: Poveš, koliko časa nekaj že traja (I've lived here for ten years, since 2016), vprašaš How long have you …? in ločiš to od tega, kar je mimo (I lived in Leeds for five years).
goal.de: Du sagst, wie lange etwas schon dauert (I've lived here for ten years, since 2016), fragst How long have you …? und trennst es von dem, was vorbei ist (I lived in Leeds for five years).
goal.it: Dici da quanto tempo dura qualcosa (I've lived here for ten years, since 2016), chiedi How long have you …? e lo distingui da ciò che è finito (I lived in Leeds for five years).
goal.en: You can say how long something has gone on (I've lived here for ten years, since 2016), ask How long have you …?, and set it apart from what is over (I lived in Leeds for five years).

say.sl: **I've lived here for ten years**: kar se je začelo nekoč in še traja, gre v present perfect. (Tu živim deset let.) **Mrs Birkett has run the inn since 2011.** (Gospa Birkett vodi gostilno od leta 2011.) Slovenščina reče sedanjik, angleščina have, has + deležnik. **I live here** pove samo, da živiš tu zdaj.
say.de: **I've lived here for ten years**: Was früher begonnen hat und noch andauert, steht im present perfect. (Ich wohne seit zehn Jahren hier.) **Mrs Birkett has run the inn since 2011.** (Mrs Birkett führt das Gasthaus seit 2011.) Deutsch sagt Präsens, Englisch have, has + Partizip. **I live here** sagt nur, dass du jetzt hier wohnst.
say.it: **I've lived here for ten years**: ciò che è iniziato nel passato e dura ancora va al present perfect. (Vivo qui da dieci anni.) **Mrs Birkett has run the inn since 2011.** (Mrs Birkett gestisce la locanda dal 2011.) L'italiano usa il presente, l'inglese have, has + il participio. **I live here** dice solo che adesso vivi qui.
say.en: **I've lived here for ten years**: what began in the past and still goes on takes the present perfect. **Mrs Birkett has run the inn since 2011.** Have or has + the participle, where your language may say the present. **I live here** only says you live here now.

say.sl: **for** + koliko časa: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages** (že celo večnost). **since** + kdaj se je začelo: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since Easter**. Vprašaj se: dolžina ali začetek?
say.de: Deutsch hat für beides *seit*, Englisch zwei Wörter. **for** + wie lange: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages** (schon ewig). **since** + wann es begann: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since Easter**. Frag dich: Dauer oder Beginn?
say.it: L'italiano ha *da* per tutti e due, l'inglese due parole. **for** + quanto tempo: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages** (da una vita). **since** + quando è iniziato: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since Easter**. Chiediti: durata o inizio?
say.en: **for** + how long: **for ten years**, **for a week**, **for ages**. **since** + when it began: **since 2016**, **since Monday**, **since Easter**. Ask yourself: a length, or a starting point?

say.it: **How long have you lived here?** (Da quanto tempo vivi qui?) Risposta breve: **For ten years.** **Since 2016.** Negativo: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** (Non vedo Jack da settimane.) **It hasn't rained since Monday.**
say.en: To ask: **How long have you lived here?** A short answer: **For ten years.** **Since 2016.** To say no: **I haven't seen Jack for weeks.** **It hasn't rained since Monday.**

say.sl: **I lived in Leeds for five years**: kar je mimo, gre v past simple, tudi s for. (Zdaj ne živim več tam.) **I've lived in Keswick for five years.** (Še vedno živim tam.) Z **ago** (pred) tudi past simple: **I came here ten years ago.** Vprašanje **When did you come here?** vpraša, kdaj.
say.de: **I lived in Leeds for five years**: was vorbei ist, steht im past simple, auch mit for. (Jetzt wohne ich nicht mehr dort.) **I've lived in Keswick for five years.** (Ich wohne noch dort.) Mit **ago** (vor) auch das past simple: **I came here ten years ago.** **When did you come here?** fragt, wann.
say.it: **I lived in Leeds for five years**: ciò che è finito va al past simple, anche con for. (Adesso non ci vivo più.) **I've lived in Keswick for five years.** (Ci vivo ancora.) Con **ago** (fa) anche il past simple: **I came here ten years ago.** **When did you come here?** chiede quando.
say.en: **I lived in Leeds for five years**: what is over takes the past simple, with for too. (I don't live there now.) **I've lived in Keswick for five years.** (I still do.) With **ago**, the past simple too: **I came here ten years ago.** **When did you come here?** asks when.

say.sl: **since** lahko začne cel stavek, v njem je past simple: **I've known Jack since he was a boy.** (Jacka poznam, odkar je bil deček.) **We've had the dog since we came here.** Glagoli know, have, be so tu zelo pogosti.
say.de: **since** kann einen ganzen Satz einleiten, darin steht das past simple: **I've known Jack since he was a boy.** (Ich kenne Jack, seit er ein Bub war.) **We've had the dog since we came here.** Die Verben know, have, be sind hier sehr häufig.
say.it: **since** può aprire una frase intera, con il past simple: **I've known Jack since he was a boy.** (Conosco Jack da quando era bambino.) **We've had the dog since we came here.** I verbi know, have, be qui sono molto comuni.
say.en: **since** can open a whole clause, with the past simple in it: **I've known Jack since he was a boy.** **We've had the dog since we came here.** The verbs know, have and be are very common here.

exercises.text: — How long ___ you lived here, Mrs Birkett? — Oh, I've lived here ___ 2011. — And Harry? — He's nine, so he's lived here ___ nine years, all his life. — Have you always had the inn? — No. I ___ (work) in Penrith for five years, then I came back. — And Jack? — I've ___ (know) him since he ___ (be) a boy. — Is he here? — No, I haven't ___ (see) him for days!

translation.sl: — Odkdaj živite tu, gospa Birkett? — Oh, tu živim od leta 2011. — Pa Harry? — Devet let ima, torej živi tu že devet let, vse življenje. — Ste vedno imeli gostilno? — Ne. Pet let sem delala v Penrithu, potem sem se vrnila. — Pa Jack? — Poznam ga, odkar je bil deček. — Je tu? — Ne, že več dni ga nisem videla!
translation.de: — Wie lange wohnen Sie schon hier, Mrs Birkett? — Oh, ich wohne seit 2011 hier. — Und Harry? — Er ist neun, also wohnt er seit neun Jahren hier, sein ganzes Leben. — Hatten Sie immer das Gasthaus? — Nein. Ich habe fünf Jahre in Penrith gearbeitet, dann bin ich zurückgekommen. — Und Jack? — Ich kenne ihn, seit er ein Bub war. — Ist er da? — Nein, ich habe ihn seit Tagen nicht gesehen!
translation.it: — Da quanto tempo vive qui, Mrs Birkett? — Oh, vivo qui dal 2011. — E Harry? — Ha nove anni, quindi vive qui da nove anni, tutta la vita. — Ha sempre avuto la locanda? — No. Ho lavorato a Penrith per cinque anni, poi sono tornata. — E Jack? — Lo conosco da quando era bambino. — È qui? — No, non lo vedo da giorni!
translation.en: — How long have you lived here, Mrs Birkett? — Oh, I've lived here since 2011. — And Harry? — He's nine, so he's lived here for nine years, all his life. — Have you always had the inn? — No. I worked in Penrith for five years, then I came back. — And Jack? — I've known him since he was a boy. — Is he here? — No, I haven't seen him for days!
